title: Link building services: how to vet vendors and which link tactics work vs. get penalized
summary: Jacky Chou's SEO essay ranks link-building vendors (Indexsy first, a self-admitted plug) and explains how to vet them. It covers effective link types (niche edits, outreach, broken-link, citations, PR) versus tactics to avoid (PBNs, article directories, volume-based packages).

principles.text: Links from aged, already-authoritative pages beat fresh posts; niche edits on existing content capture that authority.
principles.quote: Since the content exists and has been in existence for months or years, this ensures that you get a link from a page or a post that has aged well and become authoritative in its own right.

principles.text: Treat unusually cheap link pricing as a red flag for low-quality links.
principles.quote: if the price is too good to be true compared to other link-building services, this could be a red flag that they might not be quality links.

principles.text: Vet any link vendor by demanding link samples and case studies before buying.
principles.quote: Always ask for some link samples and some link-building case studies.

principles.text: Big link-building agencies tend to trade quality for scale as the team grows.
principles.quote: Often, the large link-building companies decrease the quality as the team of the size increases.

principles.text: Outreach differs from spam through personalization: target specific blogs and journalists with tailored reasons to link.
principles.quote: The main difference between blogger outreach and spam is personalization, where a good blogger outreach campaign targets specific blogs and journalists.

principles.text: Skip volume-focused backlink packages and PBNs; they are manipulative and do not stand the test of time.
principles.quote: It is an obvious attempt to manipulate the search engine rankings. But unfortunately, most PBN providers will only rent links on such sites, and they will not stand the test of time.
